briefHtml:
NAV S$10,080,155 - reported -0.49% (stale baseline), recorded -0.03% d/d; essentially flat

  • Biggest mover: Asia's Thanksgiving-Day rebound with the US shut - HSI +1.19% to 22,226.88, STI +0.65% to 4,962.64, SMIC +1.3%, Tencent +1.1%, DBS +0.6%; silver futures ~$41.7 and gold ~$3,591 in early Friday Globex, holding Wednesday's reversal
  • The one thing: global pushback on the Section 301 tariffs - China threatened necessary measures, Japan protested, Singapore said it was very disappointed (up to 20% proposed); AP confirms the US-China truce now expires Jan 10, 2027 with ~$60bn of reciprocal tariff cuts agreed. US reopens today for a 1pm ET half-session

Markets

  • US: closed Thursday (Thanksgiving); Wednesday recap - Dow 50,183 +0.33% (1,100pt intraday recovery), SPX 7,186 -0.21%, Nasdaq 23,586 -0.62%; NVDA $149.30; ANT below $83 IPO; VIX 28.29; 10y ~4.85-4.87%. Friday half-session 9:30am-1pm ET
  • Asia Thu: HSI 22,226.88 +1.19% Kabutan; STI 4,962.64 +0.65% Trading Economics; DBS S$65.85 +0.63%; Tencent HK$341.00 +1.07%; SMIC HK$45.88 +1.28%; Xiaomi HK$26.60 +0.15% (holding after Q3: net profit -68% y/y to RMB3.88bn, revenue RMB107.2bn -5%)
  • Metals (Fri morning Globex, indicative): silver ~$41.7, gold ~$3,591; Wednesday spot closes silver ~$41.12 +0.8%, gold ~$3,576 +0.6% Kitco; miners Wed: GDX $73.89 +3.5%, SILJ $19.91 +4.3%, SLVP $25.84 +4.4%
  • FX: USDSGD 1.2901; USDCNY ~6.66; USDHKD ~7.84

Flags

  • 3 critical flags: SMIC -9.1% and Xiaomi -6.7% are 5-session windows anchored to 11-19 closes (actual Thu moves +1.28% and +0.15%); listed book -3.03% same artefact; recorded NAV -0.03% d/d is the truth
  • Tencent's flag cleared after Thursday's +1.1%. L46.SI Yahoo 404 - 42nd session

Insider trades

  • None found for held names in the Nov 20-27 window. Keppel REIT's only SGX item this week (25-Nov) was conference slides, not a dealing
  • SGX API still 401 (13th trading day); Wing Tai pause 15 sessions; no HKEX filings for Tencent/SMIC/Xiaomi; US holdings are ETFs

Congress trades

  • No new filings after 11/24 (Thanksgiving freeze). Freshest: House Republican (WY-1), filed 11/23 - NVDA partial sale (10/14), MSFT sales, software sales; buys in MU, TSM x2, TSLA, NVDA (4/29) Unusual Whales
  • Senate Democrat (CT), filed 11/24 - repeated buys of MH Four Winds LLC / MH Built to Last LLC private interests (clips up to $500K-1M); one stock sale: Starling Oncology Unusual Whales

Trump / policy

  • Global pushback on Section 301: China MFA - false premise, necessary measures pledged; Japan protested; Singapore's trade ministry very disappointed - our policies do not protect our domestic market or subsidize manufacturing for export; Malaysia and EU reject the premise; Vietnam negotiating; Thailand calls 18% better than feared AP via KRCG
  • Truce math: US-China truce extended two months, expires Jan 10, 2027; ~$60bn reciprocal non-sensitive tariff cuts agreed - the 301 proposals (January at earliest) land exactly on that cliff AP via KRCG
  • Capital Economics: new tariffs broadly replace rather than add to July's forced-labor duties, but keep core goods inflation firm into next year - feeds the Dec 9 hike calculus (~96-98% for 25bp)
  • Rare-earth watch today: China's gallium/germanium export-control clock for Western buyers runs to Nov 27; USCC 2026 report: China's Dy/Lu/Sc/Tb/Y exports to the US fell to zero in May 2026 Rare Earth Exchanges
  • NVDA: Huang congressional testimony next week; closed Wednesday at $149.30 below $150

Risk

  • Silver line (est., ~$41.7 x 1.2901): collateral ~S$95,500; loan ~S$56,240; equity ~S$39,300; ratio ~1.70x - stable through the holiday; -$1 silver = -S$2,293 equity
  • Singapore named on the 301 board (up to 20%) and publicly very disappointed - overhang for STI exporters, SGD, SG rates into the Jan 5 comment deadline; VNM faces the board's highest proposed rate at 35%
  • Thin-tape Friday after a VIX-35 week; FX ~35% non-SGD (USDHKD ~7.84 peg edge, USDCNY ~6.66 into the Jan 10 cliff); metals cluster still dominant; L46.SI 404 42nd session; NAV restatements continue

Alpha (signals, not advice)

  • Real assets (20%): trigger count advances - Wed hammer (session 1), Thu quiet hold above $3,550 with US shut (session 2), Friday half-session (session 3) with gold ~$3,591. If gold closes the week above ~$3,550, the mechanical trigger is satisfied - first unlevered tranche actionable next week; silver line gets nothing
  • AI bottlenecks (15%, 0% deployed): NVDA $149.30 below the $150-155 zone into testimony week; ANT below IPO - parked until post-testimony, a 2-3-session base, or the Dec 9 FOMC clears
  • Defense (15%): 10y ~4.85-4.87% - the 5.20% gate is 33-35bp away and receding on the safety bid; TLT gated AT 5.20% only

trumpWatch.title: Global pushback on Section 301 tariffs; Singapore very disappointed
trumpWatch.detail: China MFA's Guo Jiakun: overcapacity is a 'false premise', Beijing will take 'necessary measures'. Japan's Kihara: 'regrettable'. Singapore's trade ministry: 'very disappointed', noting its policies do not protect the domestic market or subsidize manufacturing for export. Malaysia and the EU reject the premise; Vietnam is negotiating; Thailand calls its 18% cap better than feared.

trumpWatch.title: US-China truce confirmed to expire Jan 10, 2027
trumpWatch.detail: AP background: the truce was extended two months and now expires Jan 10, 2027; both sides agreed tariff cuts on ~$60bn of reciprocal non-sensitive products. The 301 proposals (effect 'January at the earliest') land exactly on that cliff.

trumpWatch.title: Capital Economics: tariffs replace rather than add, but keep goods inflation firm
trumpWatch.detail: Stephen Brown: the new Section 301 rates broadly replace July's forced-labor duties rather than stacking fully, but will likely push prices higher and 'keep core goods inflation firm into next year' - feeds the Dec 9 hike calculus (~96-98% priced for 25bp).

trumpWatch.title: China gallium/germanium export-control deadline lands today (Nov 27)
trumpWatch.detail: China's gallium/germanium export-control clock for Western buyers runs to Nov 27. USCC's 2026 report to Congress: China's exports of dysprosium, lutetium, scandium, terbium and yttrium to the US fell to zero in May 2026, with licensing delays persisting despite the truce.

trumpWatch.title: Huang congressional testimony lands next week
trumpWatch.detail: Jensen Huang appears before congressional committees next week over the scandal that briefly ousted him; Trump has called a pardon 'always an option'. NVDA closed Wednesday at $149.30, below $150.
